symptom: Vendor installer says 'Unsupported OS' on a RHEL 9 compatible server
root_cause: Installer checks ID="rhel" in /etc/os-release; server has ID="ol" (compatibility is in ID_LIKE / PLATFORM_ID)
fix: Confirm vendor support for the distribution and use their supported installer or override. Never edit /etc/os-release.

root_cause: The kernel refuses access based on the file's permissions; cat only reports the answer
fix: Nothing to fix in cat. Proof: cat /etc/hostname works, cat /etc/shadow is denied (same program, different file).

symptom: Vendor agent stopped working after patching and reboot
root_cause: Patching changed GRUB's default kernel from 6.12 (UEK) to 5.14 (RHCK); agent depends on the kernel it was installed on
fix: grubby --set-default /boot/vmlinuz-<wanted kernel>, reboot, verify uname -r. Prevention: check grubby --default-kernel before rebooting.

symptom: Developer plans 96 workers because cpuinfo says '96-Core Processor'
root_cause: The 96 cores belong to the physical host; the VM has 4 vCPUs (4 model name lines)
fix: Size workers to the VM's vCPUs; 96 CPU-heavy workers on 4 vCPUs queue and make the server extremely slow.

symptom: Backup agent down after reboot in change window: unsupported kernel
root_cause: Next-boot kernel had been changed to 5.14 by patching; reboot done without comparing uname -r and grubby --default-kernel
fix: grubby --set-default /boot/vmlinuz-6.12…, verify, reboot, check uptime + uname -r + agent log. Runbook added.

symptom: Backup script works by hand, fails at night: No such file or directory
root_cause: Relative path 'cd backups'; automatic run starts in a different folder

symptom: Search for config files looked complete but missed files (e.g. /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf)
root_cause: find ran as a normal user; protected folders gave Permission denied and were skipped
fix: Search system folders with sudo find; treat Permission denied lines as a warning that results are incomplete

symptom: cat shortcut.txt: No such file or directory, although the file is listed by ls
root_cause: Broken symbolic link: its target readme.txt was renamed
fix: ls -l shows the target path; restore/rename the target or recreate the link with ln -s

symptom: App fails at startup: touch app/logs/app.log → No such file or directory
root_cause: Deployment never created the log directory app/logs; touch cannot create parent directories. Typos in the deployment (confg, app.cong) would also have broken config loading.
fix: mkdir -p app/logs; rename confg→config and app.cong→app.conf with mv; verify with the app's exact command. Prevention: mkdir -p every required folder in the deployment steps; copy-paste reviewed commands.

symptom: Web app won't start: 'port not set'
root_cause: An empty template (web.conf.new) was copied over the live web.conf (wrong direction, no -i), leaving it empty
fix: Kept web.conf.broken as evidence, restored from web.conf.bak-20260929, verified port=8080. Prevention: cp -i for configs, check FROM/TO, dated backups.

symptom: Disk almost full; shop logs accumulating daily
root_cause: No retention policy / log rotation for shop/logs, so daily logs were never removed
fix: Listed with find -mtime +7, deleted the 3 old logs with rm -i full paths, verified recent logs kept. Prevention: logrotate with 7-day retention, disk alert at ~80%, confirm compliance retention before deleting.

root_cause: Shop lost its database connection (db01:5432) 19:42:10–19:44:30 KSA; order 1005 failed. Underlying cause lies on db01 (to be investigated by DB team).
fix: Confirmed recovery: 'database connection restored' 19:44:30 and order 1006 succeeded 19:45:02 KSA. Converted UTC→KSA (+3).

symptom: Disk usage +300 MB overnight; team's ls found nothing big
root_cause: Report job left a full export in a hidden temp folder (reports/tmp/.cache) and never removed it; plain ls hides dot-folders so it went unnoticed
fix: find -size +100M located it; owner confirmed; rm -i; same find returned nothing. Prevention: job cleans its temp files, scheduled cleanup, use find / ls -la, disk alert.

symptom: After a 'backup', /etc/ssh/sshd_config was missing; sshd -t: No such file or directory
root_cause: Backup made with mv instead of cp -p, moving the live SSH config away; the restore then used a one-character typo (sshd.config instead of sshd_config)
fix: Renamed back to sshd_config, proper backup with cp -p (sshd_config.bak-20261004), validated with sshd -t, confirmed with a new SSH login while keeping the old session open. Prevention: cp -p for backups, copy-paste critical paths, sshd -t before any restart, keep a session open until a new login works.
